text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Parliament said companies and private individuals implicated in the "Oilgate" case did not violate the law.
- The Parliament passed an act on patient's more liberal access to health data.
- Opposition parties walked out from a social and health committee meeting asking for a comprehensive debate of the pension reform plan.
- Smallholder president Jozsef Torgyan repeatedly described the government coalition as liberal-bolshevik.
- No member of the Democratic Forum's parliamentary group is affected in any way by the act on secret agents.
- Italy supports Hungary's and Slovenia's EU and NATO acccession bid, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said in Budapest.
- EU representatives told Hungary that the intergovernmental conference dealing with EU institutional reforms will be completed at the Amsterdam summit of member countries on June 16-17.
- President Arpad Goncz met King Tuanku Jaafar of Malaysia.
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy told Parliament that improvement in the economic balance appears to be a lasting trend.
- Helath insurance officials said the social security budget will almost certainly need to be supplemented.
- There is no need for a panic-driven crisis management in agriculture, said Minister of Agriculture Frigyes Nagy.
- A group of speculators are said to be behind the Postabank share swap offer.
- Budapest's fifth district council has closed down for 90 days a restaurant that charged a Danish tourist over one million forints for a dinner for four.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The enthusiasm of foreign investors in Hungary has grown over the past 18 months, said privatisation minister Judit Csiha.
- Foreign financial institutions may finance 60% of the Ft 100 billion needed for the construction of a fourth metro line in Budapest.
- Budapest Electricity Works (Elmu) has outstanding claims against customers of nearly Ft 8 billion, mainly from late or non-payment of bills.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Magyar Export-Import Bank (Eximbank) has Ft 27 billion at its disposal this year for export financing and guarantees, as compared to Ft 12 billion last year. -- Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040
